clue.text: City transit protector's back half not opening when twisted

indicators.note: the rear half of the word loses its first letter, so something is dropped from the start of that half
a thing twisted round faces the other way, so those letters run backwards

blocks.note: a seat belt protects a passenger in transit

explanation.surface: A safety device on a city bus or train is coming apart at the back, its rear twisted and broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transit' suggests buses and trains, but it is any journey in a car; the protector is split into two halves and only the back half is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a large port city in Washington State in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Cruel fact: you need to get rid of tattoo for promotion

indicators.text: you need to get rid of
indicators.note: an instruction to remove one piece from the word so that something else can take its place
one thing given for another is exchanged, so the new piece stands where the old one was

blocks.note: a statistic is a numerical fact
tat is informal shorthand for a tattoo
an ad, or advertisement, promotes a product

explanation.surface: Someone is told the harsh truth that the tattoo must go if they want to be promoted at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In STATISTIC the TAT is swapped for AD, giving S + AD + ISTIC = SADISTIC. 'Promotion' reads as a job advancement but means advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadistic person takes pleasure in inflicting pain on others, which is the essence of cruelty.

clue.text: An old hand inhabits stage part

indicators.note: to inhabit is to live inside something, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: an old hand is an experienced professional, a pro
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran actor makes a section of the theatre stage their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hand' reads as an aged limb, but it is an experienced person; the indefinite article is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the apron is the section of the stage that projects forward of the curtain toward the audience.

clue.text: Picnic-goer rearranged derby date

indicators.note: something rearranged has its parts put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone planning a day out has had to move their trip to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picnic-goer' points to the children's song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic', in which the toys go to the woods for a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical definition: the well-known song has toy bears gathering for a picnic, so one of them is a picnic attendee.

clue.text: Hip neighbour shunning lead singer

indicators.note: shunning the lead means avoiding the front, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: the pelvis is the bone structure next to the hip joint

explanation.surface: A trendy person living next door refuses to be the frontman of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' reads as fashionable but is the body part; PELVIS minus its first letter gives ELVIS, fitting for a singer famed for his swinging hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the hugely famous American rock and roll singer known as the King.

clue.text: Took a shot, weapon almost being dead

definitions.note: past-tense verb phrase, matching the answer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a gun is a weapon
esse is Latin for being or existence, a crossword staple
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A gunman fired, his weapon nearly killing somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a shot' sounds like firing a gun, but it means making a guess. GU + ESSE + D builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a shot at something is an idiom for attempting an answer without being sure, which is what guessing means.

clue.text: Information about hackneyed detective movie

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
hackneyed ideas are old and stale
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses the facts of a tired, clichéd detective film.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information. 'Detective movie' looks like a genre, but the detective is a private eye and the movie is a Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: GoldenEye is the 1995 James Bond film starring Pierce Brosnan, so it is a movie title.

clue.text: Stock online joke?

blocks.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a share price is some kind of internet gag.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: a joke posted online would be an 'e-quip', like an e-mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a kitchen or a ship is to supply it with what it needs, which is to equip it.

clue.text: Afraid to bring up a bully who's beyond reproach

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun phrase: someone or something that is beyond criticism

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing a letter up means moving it higher, so the order of the letters changes

blocks.note: scared means afraid
to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them

explanation.surface: Someone is too frightened to confront a tormentor who seems untouchable.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: in a down answer, bringing the A up means lifting it one place higher in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idiom for a person, idea or institution held to be immune from criticism.

clue.text: T S Eliot ignoring content editor's rising hate

indicators.note: ignoring the content of a word means skipping its inside, keeping only its outer letters
in a down answer something rising reads from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: taken as written: the poet's initials
first and last letters of the surname
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor, finding T S Eliot's poems empty, grows to loathe them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like the adjective meaning happy, but it is the noun: what is inside the surname. The pieces are joined first, then the whole lot reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to dislike it intensely, a direct synonym for the verb to hate.

clue.text: Russian's certainly left-wing, with wicked alter ego

blocks.note: da is Russian for yes
red is a common label for left-wing politics
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A Russian is definitely a leftist, and has a sinister secret double life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alter ego' looks like a hint at a villain, but the answer is a superhero identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevil is the Marvel superhero identity of the blind lawyer Matt Murdock, his costumed second self.

clue.text: Complete set of countries pressing to drop borders

indicators.note: dropping the borders of a word removes its edges, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the UN, or United Nations, is a body of member countries
a pressing need is an acute one

explanation.surface: A full group of nations is pushing to scrap their frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' sounds like national frontiers to fit the countries, but it means the outside letters of ACUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut film or book has nothing edited out, so it is the whole, unabridged version.

clue.text: Both sides of strategy for Alexander

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its two ends, the first letter and the last

blocks.note: the first and last letters, read as one and the other

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great's strategy is viewed from both angles.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of the word are S and Y, and saying 'S and Y' gives the answer, with the AND supplied by 'both'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy is a traditional Scottish pet form of the name Alexander, like Alex or Sasha.

clue.text: Pares back - not as much as 1A resident?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to pare fruit is to peel it
less means not as much

explanation.surface: Someone trims their spending back, wondering whether a Seattle resident has less still.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the film 'Sleepless in Seattle', so someone living in 1 Across (SEATTLE) can be described that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition borrowing the film title: in the 1993 romantic comedy, the hero is sleepless in that city.

clue.text: Tiger cub selected for shaving struggles and leaves

indicators.note: shaving trims off the edges, so a word loses its first and last letters
things that struggle thrash about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its ends are trimmed

explanation.surface: A young tiger chosen to be shaved fights back and then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: SELECTED loses its S and D to leave ELECTE; with TIGERCUB that makes the letters to mix. 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg lettuce is a crisp salad vegetable eaten as a head of tightly packed green leaves.

clue.text: Fit to choose the Spanish city lodge

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
EC is the postcode for the City of London
to table a motion is to lodge it formally

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to pick a Spanish city to stay in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a place to stay but is the verb: to lodge or table a proposal. The City of London is postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An electable candidate is suitable to be voted in, so they are fit for voters to choose.

clue.text: Karate achievement that you can't build on?

definitions.note: a relative clause describing land, standing for a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a coloured grade awarded in martial arts
second meaning: protected countryside around a town

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a dead-end award with no next step; in Britain it means land around cities protected from development.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an intermediate martial arts grade and the British zone of open land where building is restricted.

clue.text: One's working with you, at first, to undermine trial evidence

indicators.note: at first points to the very beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
in a down answer, to undermine is to go underneath, so these pieces sit below what follows

blocks.note: a test is a trial
'one is working' becomes 'I'm on', as an actor on stage
the first letter

explanation.surface: A collaborator, working with you, sets out to sabotage the evidence at a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like a court case to match the evidence, but here it is a test, which sits on top of I'M ON and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is a witness's statement given in court, a form of evidence offered in a trial.

clue.text: Go before disrupting leadership of Anthony Eden etc.

indicators.note: the leadership of a word is at its front, so only the first letter is kept
disrupting throws things into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the first letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants to act first and upset Anthony Eden's tenure as Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s, so 'leadership' looks political; here it simply means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede in time or order, coming earlier than something else.

clue.text: Musician who played with Grieg's genre

indicators.note: something played with is toyed and fiddled with, so its letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer once played in the same style as the Norwegian composer Grieg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like a relative pronoun linking the musician to the rest, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American composer and pianist behind Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess.

clue.text: Number one did shift after work

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind another in sequence

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one
to shift food is informal for eating it

explanation.surface: The top employee put in an extra shift after their usual work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a numeral but a thing that numbs. 'Shift' in the sense of polishing off food gives the past tense ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug that dulls pain and sensation, so it is literally something that numbs.

clue.text: Mood of soft stringed instrument reflected a new church

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
the lute is a stringed instrument
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The gentle atmosphere of a lute's music echoes around a newly built church.
explanation.walkthrough: P + ETUL + A + N + CE. 'Mood' suggests atmosphere, but it is the sulky kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is a sulky, irritable temper, and a mood can mean a fit of bad temper.

clue.text: Big city about to host golf

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
re means about or concerning
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A major city is preparing to stage a golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big city' looks like a single phrase, but 'Big' is the definition and the city is Los Angeles; golf is the phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and big are everyday synonyms describing something of considerable size.

clue.text: Shows part of Sussex positively

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A region of the English county of Sussex makes a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county on England's south coast. 'Shows' reads as a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are exhibitions or trade fairs, the kind of public event also called a show.

clue.text: Low-budget festival recalled after happening

indicators.note: something called back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards
coming after places one piece behind another in sequence

blocks.note: in means fashionable or happening
Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: A cheap music festival is remembered once it has taken place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happening' looks like an event taking place, but it means trendy, giving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie films or records come from independent producers, usually made with small budgets outside the major studios.

clue.text: A nymph from the underworld avoiding a goddess

indicators.note: coming up from below in a down answer means reading from the bottom upward, so the order flips
avoiding something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a naiad is a water nymph
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A spirit emerges from Hades and steers clear of a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: A + NAIAD reads upward as DAIANA; removing the A after D leaves DIANA. 'Underworld' suggests Hades, but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon, counterpart of the Greek Artemis.

clue.text: Warning of red room missed by companion

indicators.note: something missed by another is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a chamber is a room
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A guest is warned about a room painted red that their partner has not seen.
explanation.walkthrough: On British traffic lights amber comes before red. 'Red room' looks like a phrase but 'red' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic lights the amber light shows just before the red one, warning drivers to stop.

clue.text: Intelligence and super-intelligence Republican's taken from historical period

indicators.note: something taken from a whole is removed from it, so letters drop out

blocks.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a supernatural kind of knowing
R is the abbreviation for Republican
the Iron Age is a prehistoric era

explanation.surface: A sly comment that a politician's brainpower has been removed from the history books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' sounds like brains but means spying; the historical period is a prehistoric age that loses its Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of gathering secret information about enemies is espionage, the work of spies.

clue.text: E.g. tin soldiers in revolutionary set

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run the other way
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: soldiers are men in crosswords, as in officers and men
a tele is a television set

explanation.surface: Toy tin soldiers are arranged in a rebel formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin soldiers' looks like one phrase, but 'E.g. tin' is the definition. 'Set' is a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a chemical element, so it is an example of one, as the e.g. signals.

clue.text: Odds certainly shortened without fighting Trojan horse?

indicators.note: shortening cuts something off the end, so the last letter is lost
without in its old sense means outside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
yes means certainly
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A bookmaker cuts the odds on a racehorse named Trojan that will race without a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is bookmakers' shorthand for starting price. 'Trojan horse' is not the Greek trick but malicious software; the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan horse is malicious software disguised as harmless, and some kinds secretly gather data, which makes them spyware.
